description: One screen answering: is the Kafka cluster healthy, how much traffic does it carry, and which broker, topic or consumer group needs attention. Every tile links to the deep-dive dashboard.

panels.description: Brokers registered and unfenced according to the active controller. Should equal the number of brokers you run; a lower value means a broker is down or fenced (check Kafka Pods & Nodes).
panels.title: Active brokers

panels.description: Number of nodes that currently act as KRaft active controller. Exactly 1 is healthy; 0 means no metadata changes are possible (no leader elections!), 2 means a split brain during an election.
panels.title: Active controller

panels.description: Partitions without a leader (reported by the active controller). Anything above 0 means data in those partitions can be neither written nor read.
panels.title: Offline partitions

panels.description: Partitions whose followers are not all in sync, summed over the selected brokers. Short blips during restarts are normal; a persistent value means a broker or disk is too slow.
panels.title: Under-replicated

panels.description: Partitions with fewer in-sync replicas than min.insync.replicas. Producers using acks=all get NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS for them — this is an outage for writers.
panels.title: Under min ISR

panels.description: 99th percentile end-to-end latency of the KMinion probe (produce with acks=all, then consume). Green < 0.5 s, red > 2 s. The best single number for 'does Kafka work for applications right now'.
panels.title: Probe roundtrip p99

panels.description: Records produced per second across the selected brokers (client traffic only).
panels.title: Messages in

panels.description: Bytes produced per second across the selected brokers (client traffic, before replication).
panels.title: Bytes in

panels.description: Bytes fetched per second by consumers across the selected brokers (replication excluded).
panels.title: Bytes out

panels.description: Messages not yet consumed, summed over all consumer groups (KMinion). Absolute numbers depend on throughput; watch the trend in the sparkline and open Consumer Groups & Lag for time-behind estimates.
panels.title: Total consumer lag

panels.description: Partitions and topics in the cluster (from the controller's metadata image). Each partition replica costs broker memory and file handles; a few thousand per broker is fine.
panels.title: Partitions / topics

panels.description: Idle share of the request handler (I/O) threads on the busiest selected broker. Below 40 % the broker gets busy; below 20 % requests queue up and latency rises. Fix: more brokers, num.io.threads, or less load.
panels.title: Min request handler idle

panels.description: Records appended per second on each broker (leader side, replication not included). Healthy: roughly equal across brokers. A broker far above the others owns hot partition leaders — check 'Leaders per broker' and the Topics dashboard. Click a series for the broker deep dive.
panels.title: Messages in per broker

panels.description: Client traffic per broker: produced bytes above the axis, bytes fetched by consumers below (replication excluded). Out > in is normal (several consumer groups read the same data). A sudden drop of 'out' with stable 'in' means consumers stopped — see Consumer Groups & Lag.
panels.title: Bytes in (up) / out (down) per broker

panels.description: The ten topics receiving the most produced bytes right now (all brokers). Use it to find the topic behind a traffic spike. Click a bar to open the topic in Topics, Partitions & Storage.
panels.title: Top topics by bytes in

panels.description: Bytes copied between brokers to keep follower replicas in sync (in = this broker fetching as follower). Roughly (replication factor − 1) × bytes in. Spikes without more client traffic mean a broker is catching up after a restart or a reassignment is running.
panels.title: Replication traffic

panels.description: Request rate for the main API keys across the selected brokers. FetchFollower is replication; FetchConsumer and Produce are client traffic; Metadata storms (hundreds/s) usually point to a misbehaving client.
panels.title: Requests per second by type

panels.description: Partitions in trouble over time. Under-replicated: a follower is behind (broker slow or down). Under min ISR: producers with acks=all are being rejected. Offline: no leader, the partition is unavailable. Healthy: all zero. Open Broker Deep Dive → Replication to find the slow broker.
panels.title: Partition health

panels.description: How often replicas leave (shrink) and re-join (expand) the in-sync replica set. Occasional pairs after a restart are normal; a steady shrink/expand flapping means a broker or the network cannot keep up (replica.lag.time.max.ms exceeded).
panels.title: ISR shrinks / expands

panels.description: Responses with an error code other than NONE, per request type and error. NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER bursts are expected during leader moves; persistent errors (e.g. NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS, REQUEST_TIMED_OUT, UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION) need action.
panels.title: Error responses by request and error code

panels.description: 99th percentile of the total time a produce request spends in the broker (queue + local write + waiting for replicas with acks=all + response). Healthy on SSDs: < 50 ms; > 200 ms producers will notice. Open Broker Deep Dive → Request time breakdown to see which phase grows.
panels.title: Produce latency p99 per broker

panels.description: 99th percentile of the total time of consumer fetch requests. Includes fetch.max.wait.ms (default 500 ms) when there is no new data, so a flat line at the client's max wait (Java default 500 ms, franz-go 5 s) is NORMAL on quiet topics. Values above the max wait, or a high local time on Broker Deep Dive, indicate slow disks or overloaded threads (alert KafkaFetchLatencyHigh uses the local phase for this reason).
panels.title: Consumer fetch latency p99 per broker

panels.description: One row per broker (instant values). Leaders should be balanced; under-replicated > 0 or low idle values point to the broker to investigate. Click a broker id for the deep dive.
panels.title: Brokers at a glance

panels.description: Total messages not yet consumed per consumer group (sum over its partitions, from KMinion). The bar colour turns yellow at 1 000 and red at 10 000 messages. Click a bar for per-partition lag, growth rate and time-behind.
panels.title: Consumer lag by group

panels.description: Time for a KMinion probe message to be produced (acks=all) and consumed back again, p50 and p99. This is what an application experiences. Healthy: p99 < 100 ms on an idle cluster. Missing data means the probe itself is failing — see End-to-End Probe.
panels.title: End-to-end probe latency
